en.title: Germany: industrial conversion, fiscal rearmament and the reconstruction of Europe's manufacturing centre
en.deck: Germany's 2026 challenge is to convert industrial depth, savings and a much larger public-investment envelope into energy, infrastructure, defence, technology and labour productivity before demographic and external constraints intensify.
en.regime: Industrial conversion under a new fiscal-security regime: strong manufacturing capabilities and European integration coexist with weaker legacy export assumptions, ageing, energy-system reconfiguration and an execution-intensive public investment cycle.
en.key_risk: Larger public balance-sheet capacity fails to become physical infrastructure and productive private investment quickly enough to offset industrial restructuring, labour scarcity and higher security costs.
watch: Private capital formation and execution of the €500bn infrastructure programme
Automotive, machinery and chemicals output, employment and export share
China import dependence and US/China export diversification
Grid connections, storage, transmission and delivered industrial energy costs
Working-age population, migration integration, participation and productivity
Domestic capacity created by defence procurement rather than headline expenditure

pt-BR.title: Alemanha: conversão industrial, expansão fiscal e reconstrução do centro manufatureiro europeu
pt-BR.deck: O desafio alemão em 2026 é converter profundidade industrial, poupança e um orçamento de investimento muito maior em energia, infraestrutura, defesa, tecnologia e produtividade do trabalho antes que restrições demográficas e externas se intensifiquem.
pt-BR.regime: Conversão industrial sob novo regime fiscal e de segurança: capacidades manufatureiras e integração europeia coexistem com enfraquecimento das antigas premissas exportadoras, envelhecimento, reconfiguração energética e ciclo de investimento público intensivo em execução.
pt-BR.key_risk: A maior capacidade de balanço público não se converte em infraestrutura física e investimento privado produtivo com rapidez suficiente para compensar reestruturação industrial, escassez de trabalho e maiores custos de segurança.

selection_rationale: Revision 1 materially deepens the already published Germany dossier after editorial review found the first edition too compressed for the country's structural importance. The revision adds historical path dependence, trade asymmetry with China and the United States, automotive and Mittelstand adjustment, labour institutions, migration capacity, regional mechanisms, financial transmission, technology, and an explicit contradiction ledger while preserving the original country-context ID.
contrary_evidence: Germany retains exceptional industrial density, a large skilled workforce, high savings, deep EU market access and a persistent external surplus, arguing against a simple deindustrialization or decline thesis.

Larger fiscal authorizations and renewable capacity do not by themselves establish higher productivity or lower delivered industrial energy costs; execution, grids, private investment and sectoral restructuring remain binding.
limitations: The 2026 GDP, employment, trade and fiscal observations remain subject to revision.
Defence totals differ across federal-budget, constitutional and NATO definitions and are kept analytically separate.
National averages obscure large differences across Länder, municipalities and industrial clusters.
Long-run demographic projections are conditional scenarios; migration, participation, retirement behaviour and productivity can materially alter outcomes.
The report evaluates announced fiscal capacity separately from realized construction and productive capital, because appropriations are not evidence of completed assets.
